interpretation: Eight heads are competitive with the six-head baseline under this frozen 5k budget: best likelihood improves by only 0.1600%, final likelihood by 0.2474%. The curves cross (10 of 20 matched points favor E07), so this is not a consistent stepwise advantage. Peak allocated memory increases and the budget-matched training counter is slower; session/recovery/export conditions prevent an isolated speed claim. Greedy looping worsens in the fixed grid, and grammar remains weak under sampling. E06 four heads has a lower verified endpoint loss in this seed. These findings do not justify adopting eight heads or combining factors; additional authorized seeds and explicit generation diagnostics are needed. No head-diversity mechanism is inferred.
